title: Microbatch policy compiler and safety roller for continuous KV-aware batching sweeps
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Build a microbatch policy compiler that consumes continuous workload profiles and telemetry to emit ranked batching+KV-cache configuration candidates, plus a safety roller that runs shadow/apply-canary/rollback steps automatically. Goals: reduce per-token cost across mixed workloads by safely increasing coalescence and prefix cache utilization while protecting tail latencies and request correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Policy compiler produces top-3 candidate configs for a workload fingerprint within 10 minutes of profile ingestion
Shadow apply path runs without affecting production traffic and reports a deterministic diff of latency/cost/quality metrics
Canary rollout flow can be scheduled with percent traffic ramps and aborts automatically based on SLO/quality gates
Rollback triggers and automated revert complete within configured SLA (5 minutes) and restore baseline metrics
End-to-end integration tests (simulated traffic) show <=1% regressions in 95th/99th latencies for safe candidates and >=8% token-cost reduction on average for targeted cohorts
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console rollout UI
implementation_notes: Input: continuous profile stream (per-route histograms, KV hit rate, sequence length distribution, inter-arrival times)
Compiler: rule-based + small ML ranker. Start with heuristic rules derived from existing batching lab results; augment with lightweight gradient-boosted ranker for prioritization
Safety roller: shadow -> canary -> staged ramp -> monitor. Implement aborts at each stage. Snapshot config changes and keep changelog for audit
Compatibility: only propose changes compatible with pinned model variants and quantization profiles. Provide compatible fallback mapping (e.g., fallback to lower coalescence or smaller batch sizes)
Telemetry hooks: new telemetry tags for candidate_id, shadow_id, canary_id to tie metrics back to proposals
Simulation harness: replay captured traffic on a staging runtime to predict impact before canary
PRs: separate PRs for compiler core, safety-roller controller, telemetry + Console wiring
